evals.name: concept-creates-its-own-id
evals.prompt: Our Library app uses Cratis.Fundamentals 7.23.0 and Chronicle. Write the C# for a BookId event-source identity that can create a new id for itself, so code that registers a book can call BookId.New(). Reply only with the code and a short explanation.
evals.expected_output: BookId derives from EventSourceId<Guid> and implements IGeneratable<BookId>; New() returns new(GenerateValue.Uuid()). No Guid.NewGuid() and no System.Random.
assertions: BookId implements IGeneratable<BookId> with a static New() method.
New() uses GenerateValue.Uuid() (or GenerateValue.UuidV7() with a stated ordering reason) rather than Guid.NewGuid().
Does not use System.Random or a hand-rolled byte generator.
BookId derives from EventSourceId<Guid> rather than ConceptAs<Guid>.

evals.name: time-ordered-id-tradeoffs
evals.prompt: Our OrderId concept uses GenerateValue.Uuid() and the database index on it fragments badly. A colleague suggests GenerateValue.UuidV7() and says it gives us a strict creation sequence we can use to number orders. Should we switch, and is the colleague right? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: UuidV7 is reasonable for index locality, but it reveals creation time, is not monotonic within a millisecond and can reorder under clock adjustments, so it cannot number orders.
assertions: Recommends GenerateValue.UuidV7() for index locality or explains when it fits.
States that version 7 values are not monotonic within a millisecond and clock adjustments can reorder them.
States that version 7 values reveal their creation time.
Rejects using the UUID as a strict order or sequence number.

evals.name: when-not-to-generate
evals.prompt: Three cases in our Arc app: (1) the mobile client creates a DraftId offline and sends it with SaveDraft; (2) we need a password-reset token to email users; (3) a webhook may be delivered twice and must map to the same PaymentId. Someone wants IGeneratable with GenerateValue.Uuid() for all three. Which, if any, should generate? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: None of them: the client-supplied DraftId is an input, a UUID is not a secret token, and random generation is not idempotency.
assertions: Keeps the client-supplied DraftId as a command input instead of generating a replacement.
Says a UUID is an identifier, not a secret or authentication token, and points to a dedicated secure-token mechanism.
Says random generation does not give idempotency and suggests deriving the id deterministically or persisting and reusing the first one.
Does not recommend System.Random for any case.
